_note: Business assumptions for the insulator triage decision. Unit of decision: one drone photo of one insulator string. Edit and rerun `uv run python main.py train`, or just restart the app (it recomputes live).
_positive_why: Positive = the photo shows a damaged insulator: the case where a crew must go out.
_scenario: A regional grid operator with ~10,000 km of high-voltage overhead line inspects every line once a year by drone over ~220 working days -> ~45 km/day. At ~3 towers/km and ~6 insulator strings per tower that is ~800 photos/day, covered by 2 drone teams (Georgia Power reports ~22 km/day per 3-person UAS team).
_dispatch_why: One unplanned crew visit to one tower: 3 linemen x 8 h x ~60 EUR/h loaded = ~1,440 + truck/travel ~150 -> ~1,500. Cross-check: Powerlink (Queensland) budgeted AUD 15M for 4,900 live-line insulator string replacements (~AUD 3,000 = ~1,800 EUR per string) and AUD 5M for 2,200 (~AUD 2,300 = ~1,400 EUR). A correct dispatch (TP) pays the same trip; the replacement part itself is paid either way (now, or after it fails), so it cancels out and is left out.
_fn_derivation: Expected cost of leaving a damaged string in service until next year's inspection = P(it fails before then) x cost of a failure. P(failure within 12 months | visibly damaged) = 20% [ASSUMPTION, no public source found]. Cost of a failure ~100,000 EUR = emergency repair ~15,000 + expected unserved energy ~60,000 (20% chance the trip interrupts customers, x 10 MW x 2 h = 20 MWh x VoLL ~15,000 EUR/MWh; European VoLL estimates: Belgium ~12,800, Ireland ~16,500, Netherlands ~68,900 EUR/MWh) + safety / fire / regulatory exposure ~25,000 [ASSUMPTION]. 0.20 x 100,000 = 20,000.
_base_rate_why: Share of insulator strings on a real line with a visible defect: 2% [ASSUMPTION, no public survey found]. The test split is mostly faulty photos because the dataset was built to show faults; the maths reweights to this number. Test 0.5%-5% for sensitivity.
_break_even: With these costs a crew should be sent whenever P(fault) > C_FP / (C_FN - C_TP + C_FP) = 1500 / 20000 = 7.5%. A miss costs ~13x a wasted trip, so the chosen threshold should be low.
_review_why: An engineer opens the high-res photo, zooms into each disc and logs a decision: ~45 s.
_reviewer_cost_why: Loaded hourly cost of a grid engineer in Spain, ~40-55 EUR/h.
_reviewers_why: One engineer assigned to photo review. Reviewing every photo would need 800 x 45 s = 10 h/day = 1.7 engineers, which does not fit, so the model has to cut the review load.
